McLaren.summary: McLaren’s aero package gets a quick tweak: the rear diffuser has been reshaped to smooth the airflow underneath the car, and the brake‑duct winglets have been rearranged to clean up the flow at the back corners. Both changes should give the car a bit more grip and stability when exiting high‑speed turns, helping the team extract extra lap time and defend better in today’s tight circuit.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has tweaked the rear wing – straightening and shortening the top flap and lightening it – plus they’ve slimmed down the lower beam wing. All of these changes shave drag, so the car will be quicker on the straights and can carry a bit more speed into corners. In short, the new aero package should give Ferrari a better balance between straight‑line pace and corner‑exit grip for this weekend’s race.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has widened the central vent on the engine cover, helping the power unit stay cooler and more reliable over a demanding weekend. At the rear, the beam wing has been slimmed and its angle tweaked, giving the car a smoother rear‑end balance and a little extra grip in the corners. Together, the changes aim to keep the car running trouble‑free while squeezing out a few more tenths where it counts on the track.

Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has fitted a milder‑angle rear‑wing flap for this circuit, dialing back the “aggressiveness” of the element to keep drag in check. The tweak lets the car carry more speed down the long straights while still providing enough down‑force for the corners. In short, it’s a simple aerodynamic balance change that could boost straight‑line pace without compromising cornering grip for the weekend’s layout.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has opened up the rear wing—flattening it to cut drag—so the car can carry more speed down the long straights of this circuit. To keep the car stable after that change, the front‑wing flaps have been softened for a smoother, more balanced feel through the corners, giving the team a quicker, more predictable package for the weekend.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls have trimmed the front‑wing flap and eased the angles on both the rear wing and the lower beam wing, cutting down overall drag for this circuit. The result is a car that will be quicker on the straights while still keeping enough downforce to stay stable through the corners, giving the drivers a better balance between speed and grip for the weekend’s races.

Sauber / Audi.summary: Sauber‑Audi has trimmed the car’s aerodynamics for this weekend, fitting a low‑balance front‑wing flap and a reshaped central floor to smooth the airflow under the car. A brand‑new beam wing together with revamped rear‑wing endplates and a low‑drag rear‑wing assembly shave off drag, giving the team better straight‑line speed without sacrificing grip. In short, the package should make the car quicker on the long straights and more stable through the high‑speed corners that dominate this circuit.
